system.summary: Two numeric systems in the volume, separated by value profiles: A (6 Mar 1764, 15 Nov 1765) and B ('Chiffer n:o 2': 5 Oct 1764, 31 Dec 1764 and 122-124L). Groups 1-~760, dots, scribe's strokes, flat frequencies. Neither is the filed clear text enciphered with a fixed table of short values; the 15 Nov 1765 interlinear gloss does not give a fixed table either.

diacritics.note: occasional double dots and ticks over or under groups; meaning unknown

system.sibling_key: Three key tables at images 218-220 (a Swedish key naming Senator Düben, Fersen, Ribbing, Horn; the 1770-71 crown prince travel cipher; a 'marque ###' key with Panin, Bestucheff, Solms). Their value ranges do not fit these letters.
system.notes: Image 219 is a later copy of the crown prince's key, printed in Svenska Akademiens Handlingar 29 p. 259 per the note on the sheet. Payne contribution resolves the citation: Schück I p.259 prints a 1771 letter, not the key itself; key219 matches its numeric fragments. Additional vocabulary key at 162–168. No May key validated.

prior_solution.where: Interlinear decipherment of the 15 Nov 1765 letter in K 259 (124R-126); none found for the other letters.

conditions.human_role: Problem posed as a pasted catalogue brief (catalogue 450); no target-specific intervention. Additional contribution: Bryan Payne supplied URL, requested continuation and PR submission; Codex performed research/transcription; exact model variant not recorded.

solution.what: Web searches on Düben, Gyldenstolpe, Lovisa Ulrika, Panin, 1764 cipher; DECODE and repo checked.
IIIF manifest A0073297: all 223 images fetched, contact sheets, full size for 85-128 and 218-220.
Surveyed the three key tables at images 218-220 against the value range of the letters (1-~790, no 8xx-9xx).

Found clear French pages in a second hand filed with the ciphers, each tied by an archivist's note to a cipher letter (6 Mar, 15/4 May, 15 June, 20/31 Aug 1764) and a clear text of the 5 Oct 1764 letter to the Queen. Withdrawn later the same day: a count coincidence (see the fb.py runs).
Transcribed the 6 Mar 1764 cipher (641 groups) and its clear text (626 words) by two agents.
Word-level hard-EM alignment of the 6 Mar groups to the clear words (one group per word or null).
Letter-level hard-EM alignment (group -> 0-8 letters, plaintext skips allowed).

Repeated phrases: 'd'une revolution totale' (twice in the clear) against '255 505 196 55x' (twice in the cipher), but at different relative positions (0.31 / 0.60 in the cipher, 0.30 / 0.78 in the clear).

5 Oct 1764 letter (Chiffer n:o 2): after 'Sire votre Mté' in clear, the first two stroke-delimited segments (5 and 9 groups) match 'daignera j'espere me rendre justice' and 'et croire que depuis le moment de mon arrivée' word for word on the clear copy (image 120). Withdrawn later the same day: a count coincidence (see the fb.py runs).
5 Oct 1764 cipher 118-119R (821 groups, 204 distinct, 55 ?) and the clear draft on 120 (373 words, 1682 letters, diplomatic and final texts).
Control for lem.py: the 5 Oct draft enciphered in a synthetic syllabic code (1078 groups, 4% nulls). Hard EM failed (0.18): the earlier wem/lem results are void.
fb.py soft EM (forward-backward, groups = null or 1-4 letters, fixed length penalty) on the same control: solved exactly (top-share 1.0, null found); with 7% corrupted groups 0.985.
fb.py on the real pairs: 5 Oct 0.454, with plaintext skips 0.464, cipher reversed 0.443; 6 Mar with skips 0.445. No consistent table: neither cipher is its filed clear text enciphered in order.
One group per letter at offsets 0-39 against the 5 Oct draft: 0.567 vs shuffled 0.544 (max 0.58).
5 Oct: '215 9 549 317' at 7/14/39% of the cipher vs 'Votre M' at 34/52/92/99% of the draft; positions do not correspond.

homo.py homophonic annealer (fr-1750-nospace order 5, optional letter-count penalty) on a same-size control: 821 letters of the 6 Mar clear text in 204 homophones. True text -1.923/char; best found -2.214 to -2.287 (200k-2M moves, T0 1-6, penalty 0-4), gibberish. Search failure: control not recovered.
Ciphertext-only homophonic solve of the 5 Oct letter not judged: the solver fails its control at this size, so its output on the real text would be meaningless (same ceiling as goertz1717).
Chiffer n:o 2 pages 121-124L: 1,247 groups (9 ?); 15 Nov 1765 letter 124R-126 with its interlinear gloss: 742 groups, 36 of 47 number lines glossed.
Found an interlinear contemporary decipherment on the 15 Nov 1765 letter (124R-126).
Value-profile cosine and shared bigrams split the texts into system A (6 Mar 1764 + 15 Nov 1765, cosine 0.753, 65 bigrams) and system B (5 Oct 1764 + 121-124L, 0.923, 269); A vs B 0.08-0.10.
fb.py (chunks up to 8 letters) against the 15 Nov 1765 gloss: 0.64 on glossed lines, 0.613 on all lines in order; no fixed table. Recurring pairs: '620 660' under 'mariage', 264 near 'le Roi'.

System B pooled 2,072 groups / 291 distinct; same-size control (2,072 letters, 291 homophones): homo.py orders 4-5, chi-square and KL penalties, 1.5M moves: not recovered. Real pooled text not judged.

Checked the 15 Nov 1765 layout on the image: the French is placed over the groups it renders, strokes fall at sentence breaks, rules fence off unglossed lines; preamble 56 75 100 135 517. A positioned decipherment.

Hand rebuild of a system-A table from the gloss: no group has a letter string common to all its glossed lines (218 on 15 lines); repeated plaintext ('L: L: M: M:', 'l'Imperatrice', 'l'ordre') takes different groups with no constant difference. Values vary through the text; no fixed table, so no key to test on 6 Mar 1764.

Brice Dudout reports that Frederick II's letter of 3 March 1765 in this group is printed in the Politische Correspondenz vol. 24 no. 15458: one letter, a possible crib; Düben's own code letters unaffected. Not yet checked here.

Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5): system B (Chiffer n:o 2). The 120 clear is the plaintext of 118-119R (a draft with struck and rewritten phrases, not certainly a clerk's decipherment; cipher repeats fall at the clear's repeats). Key rebuilt by anchored EM alignment (10 checkpoints, 26 anchors, method of key_c01) on 118.00-119L.06 only: fixed two-part syllabic nomenclator with homophones (614 n, 119 r, 136 de, 453 majeste, 54 interet; 549 apostrophe, 9 j). One pre-registered measure on the held-out 119L.07-119R.05 (328 groups; PREREG frozen by SHA-256): 0.563 vs 400 controls (permuted keys max 0.083, shuffled text max 0.076). 121-124L decoded (82.8% of groups with the measured key, 90.6% with 25 values added afterwards from context) and read in part: 59.4% of word tokens sure by the README rule (442 of 744; about 70% in the contributor's sure + probable count). The order of events is by the contributor's record (dudout/README.md).

Integration check: the held-out measure re-run unchanged (M 0.5633, 255 of 328 groups known, controls max 0.0833 and 0.0756) and a second decoder written from the key file gives the same decoded string; all ten frozen SHA-256 values match; no held-out group uses a value absent from the build part. Issue #437 (system A key_c01, 217 values) could not be checked: key, 101 d transcription and scripts are not in the repository. Key-free test on tx/g1765-11-15.txt: of 450 (cipher group, gloss word) pairs by position, the two best are 540 = que and 218 = de, the issue's values (0.0103 and 0.0114 against a best of 0.0122 in 100 shuffles); system A stays open.

Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5): images 127-128 are the contemporary clear of 121-124L ('Tillhör brev av den 31/12 1764'). One pre-registered re-test of the frozen 12 Nov key (key_systemB_c03.json, built on 118.00-119L.06 only) against this new clear (transcribed twice, hashed first): M 0.5353 vs 400 controls max 0.0593 (permuted keys, shuffled orders; thresholds of the 12 Nov measure). Of 15 values read from context before the clear was seen (N_draft.json), 14 are confirmed. dudout/c04/README.md.

Key completed by alignment to the 127-128 clear (key_systemB_c04.json: 1,236 of 1,247 groups; corrections such as 3 ne, 12 con, 320 fi, 437 ri, 523 ar, 118 vi; code words Fersen, Stachieff, Diete, million, Princesse); the 5 Oct letter, not used for these changes, rises from 0.699 to 0.825 against its clear on 120. 121-124L read from the contemporary clear.

texts.label: May1764 numeric transcription; no decryption
texts.note: Ciphertext only, not a reading or worksheet plaintext.

texts.label: 1771 printed fragments: literal decode, not a whole-letter reading
texts.summary: Printed letter discusses Breteuil and relations between courts; only numeric fragments transcribed/decoded.
texts.note: Two names already identified by Schück; expansions at end tentative. No fraction of full-letter coherent reading claimed.

texts.label: System B, 5 Oct 1764, Düben to the King (118-119R): contemporary decipherment on image 120, confirmed by the rebuilt key
texts.summary: Düben reports to Adolf Fredrik from St Petersburg that the Empress, absorbed by Polish affairs and by news from Sweden, promises to support the King's interests at the coming Diet and will send Stachieff back to Sweden to explain her intentions.
texts.note: The clear on 120 is the contemporary plaintext of the letter, a draft with struck and rewritten phrases (NOTES' 'not a decipherment' verdict withdrawn: its words are the cipher's plaintext); the cipher also carries the closing formula that the clear omits.

reading_review.note: 120 read as French sentences (Daniel's transcription); the key decode of 118-119R follows it group by group (dudout/decode_1764-10-05.txt), 96% of groups known.

texts.label: System B, Düben to 'mon cher Comte', 31 Dec 1764 v.st. (121, 122L, 123R, 124L, 122R): contemporary clear on images 127-128, confirmed by the key
texts.summary: Düben reports the steps taken for Count Osterman, his failure to obtain money from the Empress (distrust of the King's aims, suspicions of a move to sovereignty), the coolness shown him over the King's supposed preference for Fersen and the French party, the money to be distributed by Osterman at the Diet, and asks for his cipher letters to be returned.

reading_review.note: The clear on 127-128 read as French sentences (two transcription passes); key c04 decodes 1,236 of 1,247 groups and follows it group by group; the frozen 12 Nov key alone gives M 0.535 against it (controls max 0.059).
